boundary_decision.status: accepted as a governed land-administration spatial unit
boundary_decision.rationale: The parcel owns register-qualified identity, geometry and boundary assertions, area, topology, source quality and lifecycle. Parties, titles, rights, addresses, buildings, surveys, planning, valuation and tax remain external masters.

decisions.disposition: accepted as register and jurisdiction qualified
decisions.rationale: Address, owner, title, label, geometry, area and map reference are mutable or non-unique and cannot replace the authoritative parcel identifier.
A parcel is a spatial unit; title, ownership, possession, rights, restrictions, responsibilities and mortgages are external legal relationships.
Legal, surveyed, mapped and occupied boundaries may disagree and none may silently overwrite the others.
CRS, axis order, coordinate epoch, transformation, dimensionality, precision and accuracy are necessary to interpret geometry and area.
Closure, overlaps, gaps, adjacency, containment and official versus calculated area require declared tolerances, methods and authority.
Subdivision, consolidation and reparcellation create or retire identities and preserve predecessor, successor, area-balance and legal-effect history.
LADM, LandInfra, InfraGML, INSPIRE, GML, GeoSPARQL and GeoJSON mappings pin versions and disclose CRS, topology, 3D and legal-semantic loss.
The approved relation ledger contains no WM-PLC-002 rows, so proposed links to legal, physical and administrative models remain draft.
